notes: The PER-POSTING DETAIL, measured 2026-11-19 with one plain GET (owner-approved), `GET https://api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/smartrecruiters/postings/744000158320111` -> HTTP 200 application/json. It is the first measurement of this response: the adapter's detail schema was written from the documentation, whose own examples are not valid JSON. The detail adds, over the list item, `jobAd.sections` (companyDescription, jobDescription, qualifications, additionalInformation — each `{title, text}` with HTML in `text`), `postingUrl` ("https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/smartrecruiters/744000158320111-senior-lead-engineering-operations-manager"), `applyUrl`, `referralUrl`, `jobId` and `active` (true); `visibility` is "PUBLIC". So the CANONICAL URL and the DESCRIPTION both come from here and from nowhere else, which is why a detail request per posting exists at all. A `creator` object ({name, avatarUrl}) is present in the live response and is the one field that can name a human; it came back EMPTY on this posting and was DROPPED from the committed file rather than stored, so no recruiter identity is committed and a future capture cannot copy an empty one by habit. Nothing else was removed. No GET was sent to jobs.smartrecruiters.com: `postingUrl` and `applyUrl` are data here, never a request target. robots.txt of api.smartrecruiters.com (committed beside this file as api-robots.txt) disallows every agent except LinkedInBot, while the documentation at https://developers.smartrecruiters.com/docs/endpoints calls the Posting API public and shows unauthenticated examples; this detail request rests on the SAME owner decision as the list one (2026-10-24 ACCEPT_RISK, "until banned"), and nothing here was retried and no header was changed. Every `creator` object (the only field naming a human) was dropped by key. E-mail addresses and phone numbers inside string values were replaced by a parser; personal NAMES in free-text descriptions cannot be found by a parser and were not redacted (records were chosen with short descriptions to limit exposure).
